source_refs.note: Chapter 2 student learning outcomes and introduction, as printed (PDF 25, printed 20).

blocks.text: By the end of this chapter, students will be able to :

items: apply problem-solving by effectively identifying, breaking down, and creating solutions for both straightforward and complex problems using a variety of computational thinking. They will further evaluate and refine their solutions, demonstrating their understanding of different computational techniques.

understand practical application of fundamental computational artifacts and algorithms. This includes the ability to explain common computational problem-solving methods and a basic comprehension of primitive computational structures like lists, stacks, queues, trees, and graphs. Moreover, students will be able to use knowledge representation and reasoning, employing propositional and predicate logic in their problem-solving.

blocks.text: In this chapter, students learn the basic concepts of logic and computational thinking used in computer science. They understand how to solve problems in a clear and systematic way. Students explore computational thinking techniques such as decomposition and step-by-step problem solving. They also study propositional logic, truth values, truth tables, and logical equivalence.

The chapter introduces satisfiable and unsatisfiable propositions and their role in decision-making. Students then learn predicate logic, variables, and quantifiers to express relationships and conditions. Finally, they develop logical reasoning and inference skills, building a strong foundation for analytical thinking and advanced computer science topics.
